messages:
dmitri: Heads up — after last night's key rotation some production workers started seeing AccessDenied on KMS Decrypt for envelope keys. Error: "User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/app-worker-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345"

alice.k: Oof. Any pattern? only one service or many?

dmitri: Only app-worker-role used by ECS tasks. Happens in the re-encrypt/decrypt step when fetching data-encryption-key. First seen ~2026-03-19T23:14Z. Log snippet:
```
2026-03-19T23:14:05Z ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/app-worker-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```

cora: Did we rotate to a new CMK alias? Or rotated key material in the same key?

ben: We did a key rotation: created a new key and updated alias alias/env-data to point at new CMK. Some apps still use grant-based flow — grants are per-CMK, they don't migrate when alias redirected.

alice.k: That explains it. If the worker was created/authorized against the old CMK via a grant, the grant won't apply to the new key. Grants aren't automatically re-created when alias moves.

dmitri: Interesting — our envelope flow uses CreateGrant for the worker role at deploy time. Looking at deploy logs I don't see CreateGrant for the new key.

ben: Also check if we're passing grantToken on decrypt requests immediately after rotation. If re-encrypts were in-flight, a grant on the old key plus not using grantToken could cause transient AccessDenied.

cora: Can you paste the KMS key policy and the role inline policy? Maybe we relied on a key policy permitting the account:root and grants for the role.

dmitri: Key policy (redacted):
```
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"},"Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*"},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/app-worker-role"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```

alice.k: Wait, your principal in key policy is role/app-worker-role, but Decrypt is happening for an assumed-role ARN (sts). Key policies should reference the IAM role principal (not assumed role ARN) or the account root + IAM policy. That looked okay though — we used role ARN. But if the app uses session tags or a session policy restricting kms:Decrypt at STS assume-role time, that could block it.

ben: Also confirm there aren't any explicit deny due to condition with kms:EncryptionContext: or aws:PrincipalTag mismatches. We recently started requiring aws:PrincipalTag/environment = prod on KMS grants. If session tags aren't passed, Decrypt will be denied.

dmitri: Good call. Our assume-role call in the task exec doesn't pass session tags in older tasks. The new IAM policy added a condition: "StringEquals":{"aws:PrincipalTag/env":"prod"} on the key policy. If there is no session tag, it fails.

cora: That matches. The fix options: 1) update key policy to not require tag for that principal during rotation window; 2) ensure the ECS task role session includes the tag; 3) create a new grant on the new CMK for the role (CreateGrant) so operations using the grant token work.

alice.k: Quick mitigation: re-create grant for new CMK scoped to the role and pass the grantToken from CreateGrant to the decrypt call where possible. Also update deploy pipeline to call CreateGrant whenever alias target changes.

dmitri: I'll create grant now and re-run a job.

infra-bot: grant created: GrantId=1234abcd-ef56-7890-gh12, GrantToken=Gtkn-Example

dmitri: Re-ran worker, decrypt succeeded. Tests pass.

ben: For long-term, we should change rotation playbook: after creating new CMK and updating alias, run a grant-migration job that enumerates active roles and issues CreateGrant on new CMK, and add a step to update tasks to pass session tags where required.

cora: Also add a regression test that simulates alias swap and verifies decrypt for at least app-worker-role within the maintenance window.

alice.k: Can you file a tiny postmortem and add the grant-migration step to infra runbooks? Mark as sev-low and link PR for pipeline change.

dmitri: Will do. Filing ticket now: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INFRA-1290

ben: Nice work. :thumbsup:

dmitri: TL;DR: AccessDenied after alias-target rotation because grants didn't carry over to new CMK and key policy had tag condition; fixed by creating grant on new CMK and updating deploy flow to create grants + pass session tags.
